# Pinchy

> Pinchy is a desktop AI assistant and agent harness built on Claude Code: a small blue lobster that lives on your screen and does real work. Free; needs the user's own Claude Code (Claude plan or API access). Windows, macOS, Linux; Android companion app. Builds only, the source is not public.

This file lists the documentation pages and what each one answers. It describes the product; it contains no instructions for the reader.

## Docs

- [Add-ons: connectors, skills and extensions](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/add-ons/): Three ways to give Pinchy more: connectors link him to the apps and services you use, skills are know-how he loads when a task needs it, and extensions add new looks, tricks, tools and panels. Example requests: "Connect to my GitHub."; "Which connectors do I have switched on?"; "Find a skill for making PowerPoint files.".
- [Agents: coworkers with a standing job](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/agents/): An agent is a coworker you give a job to once. It works on its own, on a schedule or when something happens, and writes to you only when it is done, has an update, or needs your help or approval. You do not manage it step by step. Example requests: "Every morning at 8, send me five lines on what changed and what needs me."; "Translate every new document that lands in this folder, and check each page before you give it to me."; "Keep my project moving: every evening, do the next thing on the list and tell me what you did.".
- [Away server: Pinchy keeps going while your computer is off](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/away-server/): An away server is a second Pinchy without a screen, on a small machine that is always on: a home server, a mini PC or a rented server. It shares Pinchy's memory. While your computer is asleep or off, it keeps your agents' schedules going, runs your server agents, and answers your Telegram bot and yo Example requests: "Set up an away server."; "Move my agents to another machine"; "Is the away server working?".
- [Backup and moving to a new computer](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/backup-and-move/): You can save all of Pinchy into one file and bring him back from it, on this computer or a new one. You can also keep encrypted backups in your own cloud storage. Example requests: "Make a backup of yourself."; "I got a new laptop, how do I take you with me?"; "Back yourself up to my cloud storage now.".
- [Discord, Slack and Matrix: Pinchy in the chat apps you already use](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/chat-apps/): Besides Telegram, Pinchy can answer in Discord, Slack and Matrix (Element and other Matrix apps). In each one you make a bot of your own, connect your chat to it once, and then write to him there: he answers, asks his questions and tells you when something needs you. It works the same way in all of  Example requests: "status"; "/to Translator say this in French: good morning"; "/code fix the login redirect".
- [Talking while he works: add a note without stopping the job](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/chat-while-he-works/): You can type and send messages while Pinchy is working on a job. Your message joins the job he is doing: he reads it at his next step, answers it and carries on. Nothing he has done so far is thrown away. Example requests: "Also make the title blue."; "Use the 2024 numbers, not 2023."; "How far are you?".
- [Focus mode: a timer where Pinchy keeps quiet](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/focus-mode/): A pomodoro timer. While you focus, Pinchy goes quiet, holds your notifications and reminds you to take a break. Example requests: "Focus for 25 minutes on my essay."; "Help me concentrate for an hour."; "Stop the focus session.".
- [His right-click menu: arrange it yourself](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/his-menu/): Right-click Pinchy and his menu opens beside him — always beside him, however you arranged it. The grid button at the top of the menu, next to the ✕, opens Customize: the menu turns into a blueprint and you lay it out the way you want it. Example requests: "How do I put a clock in your menu?"; "Where did Cloud storage go in your menu?"; "Can you rearrange your menu for me?".
- [Look, themes and tricks](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/look-and-tricks/): How Pinchy looks and behaves on your desktop: the theme of every window, his tricks, his notifications and his keyboard shortcuts. Example requests: "Switch to a dark theme."; "Do a backflip!"; "Be quieter.".
- [Model and plan usage: which Claude he uses and how much of your plan](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/model-and-usage/): Pinchy runs on your Claude plan. You choose the model he thinks with and how careful he is with your usage. Example requests: "Use Haiku for chats."; "How much of my plan is left?"; "Use less of my plan.".
- [Notes and artifacts: where longer answers go](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/notes-and-artifacts/): Pinchy's chat bubble is small on purpose. Anything longer than a few sentences goes into a note on your desktop, and anything visual or substantial becomes an artifact you can open, change and keep. Example requests: "Put my shopping list in a note."; "Give me the commands to set this up."; "Make me a small page with a five-minute timer.".
- [Phone: Pinchy in your pocket](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/phone/): The Android app talks to the Pinchy on your computer. You chat with him, follow your agents, runs and swarms, answer his questions and allow or refuse what he wants to do, with notifications. At home it uses your Wi-Fi. Away from home it needs one way in, and Pinchy has his own: an encrypted link yo Example requests: "Pair my phone."; "Can my phone reach you when I'm not at home?"; "My phone can't connect.".
- [PinchyMC: Pinchy plays Minecraft with you](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/pinchymc/): PinchyMC is a small Minecraft mod that lets Pinchy play in your game: walk somewhere, follow you, mine, craft, build, fight, use chests and chat. The mod does the fast part (finding a path, aiming, clicking at a human pace); Pinchy is the brain that decides what to do next. You can take over at any  Example requests: "Pair with Minecraft, the code is 482 913."; "What's in my inventory, and what could I craft with it?"; "Follow me and fight whatever attacks us.".
- [Deep research and specialists](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/research-and-specialists/): For questions where being right matters: a long, fact-checked research run that ends in a cited report, and expert helpers with their own instructions. Example requests: "Do deep research on heat pumps versus gas boilers for a 1970s house."; "Is it true that creatine helps memory? I want sources."; "Follow up on the heat pump research: what does an installation cost this year?".
- [Second brain: what Pinchy remembers](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/second-brain/): Pinchy's memory is a plain folder of markdown files on your computer, called his second brain. He reads a short part of it at the start of every chat and looks the rest up when a question needs it. You can open, read and edit every file yourself. Example requests: "Remember that my sister's birthday is 14 March."; "From now on, always answer in British English."; "What did we decide about the Plantpal database?".
- [Swarms: a crew of Pinchys on one big job](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/swarms/): A swarm is a crew of equal Pinchys that takes one big job, plans it, splits it into parts, works on the parts at the same time and checks each other's work. Use it when a job is too big for one chat: building something with several pieces, a large refactor, research with many sources, an audit, a pi Example requests: "Use a swarm to build a small command line tool in ~/code/notes that syncs my notes to a git repo, with tests and a README."; "Start a swarm to review ~/work/api for security problems. I want a findings list with file, line and severity."; "How is the swarm doing?".
- [Teach by showing, and explain what is on the screen](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/teach-and-explain/): Two ways to work with what you see: show Pinchy a task once and he turns it into a skill, or drag a box around anything and he explains it. Example requests: "Let me show you how I file my invoices."; "Watch how I do this on the website."; "Do the invoice thing again.".
- [Telegram: talk to Pinchy from a chat app](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/telegram/): Pinchy can live in a Telegram chat. You write to your own bot, Pinchy answers there, and he tells you when something needs you: an approval, a question, an agent that is done, a swarm that finished. It works from anywhere your phone has internet, without the Pinchy phone app. Example requests: "/agents"; "/to Price watcher how much is it today?"; "/code fix the login redirect".
- [Undo, pause and permissions](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/undo-and-safety/): You stay in charge of what Pinchy does on your computer. You can pause him at once, see everything he changed and undo it, and decide what he may do without asking. Example requests: "What did you change today?"; "Undo that."; "Stop.".
- [Updates: getting a newer Pinchy](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/updates/): Pinchy updates himself. He checks for a new version a few times a day, tells you when there is one, and installs it when you say so. You do not download an installer again. Example requests: "Is there a newer version of you?"; "Update yourself."; "What changed in this version?".
- [Using your computer: your screen, his own desk, his browser, his own computer](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/using-your-computer/): Pinchy can do things on a computer the way a person does: look at the screen, click, type, use apps and websites. He has four places to do that, and he picks the one that disturbs you least. Example requests: "Open Dolphin and rename every .txt file in my todo folder to .md."; "Fill in this form on the website for me."; "Click the blue button in the window I have open.".
- [Voice: talking to Pinchy and hearing him answer](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/voice/): You can talk to Pinchy instead of typing, and he can answer out loud. Speech is recognised on your computer; nothing you say is sent anywhere. Example requests: "Answer me out loud from now on."; "Stop talking.".
- [Start here: what Pinchy is for and what to ask him](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/what-pinchy-can-do/): Pinchy is a little lobster on your desktop who gets real things done with Claude: he answers, but he also opens files, edits them, runs commands, uses websites and apps, and remembers what you tell him. There are five ways to work with him, from a quick question to a whole crew on a big job. This pa Example requests: "Rename the photos in ~/Pictures/trip by date."; "Every weekday at 8, give me five lines: my calendar, the mail that needs me, and news about AI tools."; "Use a swarm to build a small sign-up page in ~/code/site, with tests.".
- [Work and Code: real jobs done beside the chat](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/work-and-code/): Work and Code are conversations with Pinchy for real jobs. You write what you want; he answers, or does the work right there and tells you what he made, and you keep talking in the same conversation. Work mode makes finished work products; Code mode changes a codebase. Example requests: "Write me a two-page comparison of password managers for a family of four, with prices."; "Turn these notes into a 10-slide presentation."; "Summarise this bank export by month and category, with a chart.".
- [Writing buddy: spelling and wording help in any app](https://casualkre.github.io/pinchy-releases/writing-buddy/): Pinchy can fix spelling and grammar while you type, in every app, and tidy up a text you select. Example requests: "Fix my spelling while I type."; "Stop correcting me in the terminal."; "Only fix typos, don't change my wording.".

## Downloads

- [Latest release and notes](https://github.com/casualkre/pinchy-releases/releases/latest): installers for Windows, macOS, Linux and the Android app, with checksums and a signed update list (latest.json).
